newsitem.title: USA: Lott urges Clinton to resist Democrat pressure.
newsitem.headline: Lott urges Clinton to resist Democrat pressure.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott Saturday urged President Clinton to resist pressure from some Democrats to veto legislation that would implement an agreement to balance the budget over five years.

Congressional leaders and the White House last month reached an agreement to balance the budget over five years, but the Clinton administration has said it does not like tax legislation that is working its way through Congress.

"We've already run into endless disputes over various details, and some of those details can amount to tens of billions of your tax dollars," Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said in the Republican radio address.
"Some members of the President's party in Congress are asking him to veto the very legislation that would carry out our agreement. I hope he won't follow their advice," Lott said.
The House Ways and Means Committee Friday approved legislation to cut taxes by $85 billion over five years to ultimately enact the tax portion of the budget agreement.
Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, is expected to unveil his tax cut plan Tuesday.
"We're going to have a tough fight on our hands," Lott said. "The pro-tax forces...they're well organised, and they're clever."
Lott said he planned to bring spending and tax bills that would implement the budget agreement to the Senate floor for a vote by the end of this month.
"The President can make it bipartisan with a clear, unequivocal stand in support of our agreement," Lott said.
